title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: in 'variations sur l'équation des lacets' Grothendieck generalizes the modular situation (SL(2,Z) seen as the amalgam generated by an order-6 element ρ and an order-4 element σ, i.e. pi_1 of the modular orbifold / M_{1,1}, related to M_{0,3}) to arbitrary pairs (ρ,σ) in GL(2). To such a pair he attaches group schemes M_{ρ,σ} ⊃ M°_{ρ,σ} over a base S, with M_{ρ,σ}/M°_{ρ,σ} ≅ μ2×μ2, and a subgroup T^!_{ρ,σ} ≅ M^!_{ρ,σ}(0). The previous page fixed, in the modular case ρ=[[0,1],[-1,1]], σ=[[0,1],[-1,0]], a canonical section τ_∞=diag(-1,1) of T^!_{ρ,σ}.

This page: (35) lists three determinant -1 involutions of GL(2,Z): r_0 = τ'_∞ = [[0,1],[1,0]], r_1 = -τ'_0 = [[-1,1],[0,1]], r_∞ = τ_∞ = diag(-1,1), referring back to p.335', §42 IV. As anti-holomorphic maps of the upper half-plane they are z ↦ 1/z̄, z ↦ 1 - z̄ and z ↦ -z̄, i.e. the reflections in the three sides (|z|=1, Re z=1/2, Re z=0) of the (2,3,∞) hyperbolic triangle. They generate the extended modular group PGL(2,Z) as a Coxeter/triangle reflection group.

One can check the pairwise products:
- r_0 r_1 = [[0,1],[-1,1]] = ρ (angle π/3).
- r_∞ r_0 = [[0,-1],[1,0]] = σ^{-1} (angle π/2).
- r_∞ r_1 = [[1,-1],[0,1]] is parabolic (cusp, angle 0).
So in the modular case ρ and σ factor through a common reflection r_0. In that sense the 'antiinvolutions' are the real structures (complex conjugations) of the modular/three-point situation.

Grothendieck asks whether, outside the modular case, one can define analogous antiinvolutions generalizing these generating reflections, and says he is convinced one can. He first recalls a subgroup μ2×μ2×μ2 of M_{ρ,σ} giving three remarkable sections (the -1 of each μ2 factor). He then corrects himself ('je me mélange les pinceaux'): those were sections of M°_{ρ,σ}, whereas τ_∞, τ'_∞, τ'_0 are 'multipliers'. A side question, with a query mark, asks whether Z_{ρ,σ} equals the centre of M°_{ρ,σ}. These multipliers have multiplier -1, so ε = ε' = -1, i.e. they lie over the 'least trivial' section (-1,-1) of M_{ρ,σ}/M°_{ρ,σ} = μ2×μ2.

A crossed-out start (36) recalls a description of T^!_{ρ,σ}:
- T^!_{ρ,σ} ≅ G_{ρ,σ}(δ) ⊂ T_0 × T_ρ × N'_σ ≅ {(u,a,b) : det u = det b = ε' det a, ε'^2 = 1}.
- T_0 ≅ G_m via the determinant.
- There are canonical injections j_ρ: G_m → T_ρ and j_σ: G_m → T_σ into the centralizer tori of ρ and σ (norm tori of Z[ζ3] and Z[i]); composed with the determinant they give λ ↦ λ^2.
The next page then computes the invariants (α, β, ε, ε', u, a, b) of r_∞ concretely.
errors: No mathematical error. Grothendieck himself flags a confusion (sections of M° vs. multipliers of M) and corrects it on the page.
The question 'Z_{ρ,σ} = Centr M°_{ρ,σ}' is left with a query mark, unverified.
Minor: τ'_∞ = [[0,1],[1,0]] has entry 0, not ∞ (the handwriting is ambiguous).

ideas.what: Three det -1 involutions of GL(2,Z) as generators: the reflections in the sides of the (2,3,∞) triangle, whose pairwise products are ρ, σ^{-1} and a parabolic element
ideas.modern_name: Extended modular group PGL(2,Z) as the (2,3,∞) Coxeter triangle reflection group
ideas.where_published: Classical; Grothendieck's own use appears in the Longue Marche manuscripts (§42 referenced)

ideas.what: Antiinvolutions as canonical real structures (complex-conjugation sections) in the profinite/Teichmüller group-scheme setting, lying over the 'least trivial' component (-1,-1) of M/M° ≅ μ2×μ2
ideas.modern_name: Complex conjugation / real structures in the GT-hat and Teichmüller tower; anti-holomorphic involutions of dessins
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld, Ihara (complex conjugation in GT-hat); Grothendieck–Malle / Esquisse on real dessins
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme mentions Gal(C/R) and real structures in passing; the details here are unpublished

ideas.what: Generalizing the modular case to arbitrary pairs (ρ,σ) in GL2 via group schemes M_{ρ,σ}, M°_{ρ,σ} and T^!_{ρ,σ}, described through tori T_0, T_ρ, N'_σ with determinant conditions
ideas.modern_name: No standard name; close to arithmetic subgroup schemes attached to torsion elements and their centralizer (norm) tori

missed.claim: Conjecture (Grothendieck 'convinced') that for general (ρ,σ), not only the modular one, there exist antiinvolutions generalizing the three generating reflections r_0, r_1, r_∞. Concretely this means det -1 involutions r_0, r_1, r_∞ with ρ = r_0 r_1 and σ^{±1} = r_∞ r_0, i.e. a common reflection r_0 inverting both ρ and σ, realized inside the group schemes M_{ρ,σ}.
missed.quote: Il serait intéressant de voir si, en dehors des cas modulaire, on peut introduire des "antiinvolutions" qui généralisent les [réflexions] génératrices ... je suis convaincu que oui.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This would give real structures / complex-conjugation analogues for Grothendieck's generalized loop-equation groups, parallel to the role of complex conjugation in GT-hat. Over a field every SL2 element is a product of two det -1 involutions, but a common factor for ρ and σ over Z or Z-hat is a nontrivial arithmetic condition. Still, this is a modest open thread.

deep.surprise_reason: The reflections generating PGL(2,Z) are classical. The novelty is only the stated conviction that antiinvolutions extend to Grothendieck's idiosyncratic M_{ρ,σ} framework, which is a small unfinished thread rather than a result.
transcription_corrections: Line in (35): the image reads r_0 = τ'_∞ (with an overwritten symbol), and the next lines read r_1 = -τ'_0 and r_∞ = τ_∞; 'Γ_1, Γ_∞' should be r_1, r_∞, consistent with the next page.
'les opérations génératrices' is more likely 'les réflexions génératrices'.
Top '503' is a page numbering; the archive page is 403.
'(Z_{ρ,σ} ≟ Centr M°_{ρ,σ})' is a side remark inserted within crossed-out text.
